title: Physics test
about: The very first playable build. One stand-in player and no racket art: just the court and a ball you can feed in to see how the arcade ball physics feels.

title: Rules and scoring
about: The rules of a rally and squash scoring, checked by automated tests. They run behind the scenes, so on screen it still plays like S1.

title: First 2-player rally
about: The first version you can really play: two players share one keyboard, with serving, turns and scoring. The players are still colored boxes.

title: Hitting and ball feel
about: Swings use the arcade's timing and you can dive for shots. After the play-test: an aimed serve, 2-second dives and smoother player sizes.

title: First CPU opponent
about: Play alone against a computer opponent that moves and hits like the arcade CPU.

title: Nine difficulty levels
about: The CPU plays very differently at each level, from slow and forgiving at level 1 to arcade-sharp at 9.
note: Needs a keyboard. Starts at level 5.

title: Gamepads
about: Play on one or two controllers, or one player on the keyboard and one on a controller.
